title: Find wasted cloud spending with a lean agent toolset
summary: Sarvar Nadaf had an agent in Kiro hunt for wasted AWS spending; after he trimmed its toolset from 15 tools to 4, he reports it needed 2 steps instead of 7.
agent_role: The agent decided which cost checks to run and assembled the findings on wasted spending. The author built and redesigned the read-only tools it could call.
outcome: Author reports the same question went from 7 tool calls to 2, with tool descriptions 88% smaller.
what_they_did: Sarvar Nadaf built a small read-only connector that lets an agent inspect an AWS account. He wired it into the Kiro coding agent and asked, "where am I wasting money in this account?" First he gave it 15 narrow tools, one per AWS lookup. Then he rebuilt it as 4 tools, including one that runs every waste check at once and returns only key fields.
how_it_went: He says the first version took seven separate lookups before answering. The rebuilt version answered the same question in two calls, and its tool descriptions shrank by 88%. Both versions are shared in one code repository.
worth_knowing: Every tool description an agent can see takes up its working memory on every turn. Many look-alike tools also make it pick the wrong one and retry, which costs more.
prompt: Using read-only access to my AWS account [account or profile name], find where I am wasting money. Check for unattached storage volumes, unused public IP addresses, old snapshots, idle servers, unused gateways and idle load balancers in [region]. For each finding, list the item, why it looks wasted and a rough monthly cost. Do not change, stop or delete anything. Show me the full list and wait for my approval before suggesting any cleanup steps.

curation.rationale: A real agent workflow that finds wasted cloud spending, with code for both versions and measured numbers. It leans toward a tool-design tutorial, which limits its appeal to non-engineers.
